case.pattern_description: Coordinated multi-card syndicate abuse utilizing a single recurring device profile behind an anonymous proxy to execute low-dollar online charges across dozens of unrelated compromised card accounts. The activity intentionally stays below automated risk thresholds and evades standard fraud model detection by spreading single or paired low-velocity transactions across accounts without traditional card-testing spikes. This coordinated operation matches multiple prior confirmed fraud cases and active syndicate ring behavior rather than isolated card-not-present fraud.

The flagged transaction amount of $36.12 is modest and represents an isolated online transaction with no subsequent charges or rapid card-testing sequence on card C02975-K1 during the two-week activity window.

Holder C02975-K1|NA|138 has zero prior transactions, so transaction 3466014 is the first observed transaction for this holder, showing no active baseline deviation while lacking established holder history.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Risk monitoring flagged an online transaction of $36.12 (transaction 3466014) on card C02975-K1 associated with customer C02975 due to association with device fraud ring 36700632. Although automated model scoring was low at 0.014, graph analysis revealed that device D004630 was utilized across 17 distinct cards within 30 days, consistently appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy. Furthermore, device D004630 was previously implicated in four confirmed fraud cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035), and card C02975-K1 previously suffered confirmed compromises in CC-3908 and CC-5345. Given the decisive cross-card syndicate activity fitting an undocumented multi-card abuse pattern, the case is escalated for regulatory reporting and ongoing monitoring of connected cards.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details coordinated unauthorized card activity involving customer C02975 and card C02975-K1. On November 17, 2016 at 20:38:00 UTC, an online card-not-present transaction (transaction ID 3466014) totaling $36.12 was authorized on card C02975-K1. The transaction was initiated online without region location data using mobile device D004630, profiled as a Samsung SM-G935F running Android 7.0 with Chrome 62.0, operating behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). Device D004630 appeared as a newly registered device for card C02975-K1 and was identified as a member of organized fraud ring 36700632. Knowledge graph analysis revealed that device D004630 was actively used to conduct transactions across 17 distinct card accounts between October 18, 2016, and November 20, 2016, including connected cards C09906-K1, C01996-K2, C04108-K2, and C10326-K1. In each instance across the 17 connected cards, device D004630 appeared as a new device operating behind an anonymous proxy, demonstrating a deliberate pattern of multi-account rotating usage. Historical case records confirm that device D004630 was previously confirmed fraudulent in four closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035) involving unauthorized online purchases. Additionally, card C02975-K1 was the subject of two prior confirmed fraud investigations under closed cases CC-3908 and CC-5345. The perpetrators appear to systematically test and exploit compromised card numbers through low-dollar online transactions designed to circumvent automated scoring thresholds. Total direct financial exposure identified on the subject card C02975-K1 is $36.12. The bank has initiated case management, flagged the connected card portfolio for monitoring, and filed this report to document the coordinated fraud scheme.

stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to Policy Section 6 because further investigative steps would not alter the decision; decisive cross-card links connecting device D004630 to an active fraud ring and multiple confirmed prior fraud cases warrant immediate reporting and card monitoring regardless of cardholder contact.
